scope: Source-level validation of the owner-approved per-tenant private CRM origin allowlist across API, Cloud and Browser.
verified_contracts: Explicit RFC1918 and loopback HTTP(S) origins are accepted; unconfigured ports/origins are denied.

URL credentials, non-HTTP schemes, query strings/fragments in configured endpoints, path-bearing allowlist entries, malformed persisted entries, and over-limit destination sets are rejected or excluded.

API and Cloud normalize and persist the same tenant vendor origins, preserve valid stored origin entries during edits, fail closed on unsafe legacy config, and omit credential/config secrets from public projections.

Browser enforces tenant scope for destinations, frames, popups, IPC navigation and network requests, including redirects and websocket requests; link-local metadata and other tenant origins are blocked.
Service-worker requests without a unique tenant scope use intersection/deny behavior rather than combining tenant allowlists.
network: No CRM, private host or customer endpoint was contacted; tests used synthetic IPs and domains only.
limitations: Source policy regression and build evidence only; no live private CRM, DNS rebinding, customer sandbox, OS network policy, or deployed runtime was tested.
Customer-specific call/CRM acceptance remains pending each customer's chosen providers and configuration.
